section: Governors-General of Bengal and of India - Warren Hastings to Dalhousie: key measures
subsections: Governor-General - wars and treaties during tenure
FIRST - Governor, Governor-General, Acts that changed the title

accepted.s: Which one of the following measures is associated with Warren Hastings?
accepted.x: Warren Hastings abolished the Dual Government in 1772. The Permanent Settlement was introduced by Cornwallis, the Subsidiary Alliance by Wellesley and Sindh was annexed during Ellenborough’s tenure.
accepted.tq: Use the ruler–measure association and reject measures belonging to neighbouring administrations.

accepted.s:
With reference to Warren Hastings, consider the following statements:
1. He shifted the treasury to Calcutta.
2. He stopped the payment of ₹26 lakh tribute to Shah Alam.
3. He established Diwani and Fauzdari Adalats.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: Warren Hastings shifted the treasury to Calcutta, stopped the ₹26 lakh tribute to Shah Alam and established Diwani and Fauzdari Adalats.
accepted.tq: Combine three measures of the same Governor-General and identify the complete code.

accepted.s: Which of the following institutions was founded by Warren Hastings?
accepted.x: The Asiatic Society of Bengal was founded during Warren Hastings’s tenure. College of Fort William is associated with Wellesley and the Public Works Department with Dalhousie.
accepted.tq: Apply the founder–institution trap by distinguishing institutions of successive administrations.

accepted.s: The Cornwallis Code of 1793 is chiefly associated with which of the following measures?
o: Separation of revenue administration from justice
accepted.x: The Cornwallis Code of 1793 separated revenue administration from judicial administration. The other measures belong to Wellesley, Bentinck and Dalhousie respectively.
accepted.tq: Identify the precise administrative reform linked with the named code.

accepted.s: Which one of the following posts was created during the tenure of Lord Cornwallis?
accepted.x: Lord Cornwallis created the post of District Judge as part of his judicial and administrative reforms.
accepted.tq: Use the post–reformer association rather than confusing it with a later office.

accepted.s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
accepted.x: Wellesley established the College of Fort William in 1800. The Anti-Slavery Act was associated with Ellenborough, while the Permanent Settlement and Cornwallis Code belonged to Cornwallis.
accepted.tq: Start with the sure institution–Governor-General pair and eliminate swapped measures.

accepted.s: The Treaty of Amritsar of 1809 was concluded during the tenure of:
accepted.x: Minto I concluded the Treaty of Amritsar with Ranjit Singh in 1809.
accepted.tq: Discriminate between similarly named or successive Governors-General through the treaty year.

accepted.s: Which one of the following statements regarding Marquess Hastings is correct?
o: He introduced the Permanent Settlement in Bengal.
He founded the College of Fort William.
He introduced the Mahalwari system in 1822 through Holt Mackenzie.
accepted.x: The Mahalwari system was introduced in 1822 through Holt Mackenzie during the tenure of Marquess Hastings. The other measures are associated with Cornwallis, Wellesley and William Bentinck.
accepted.tq: Find the single correct measure among reforms belonging to different administrations.

accepted.s: Which of the following was NOT a measure of William Bentinck?
o: Treaty of perpetual friendship with Ranjit Singh
Introduction of the Mahalwari system in 1822
accepted.x: The Mahalwari system was introduced in 1822 during the tenure of Marquess Hastings. Bentinck abolished Sati, suppressed female infanticide and concluded a treaty of perpetual friendship with Ranjit Singh in 1831.
accepted.tq: Find the measure belonging to the preceding administration rather than the named Governor-General.

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements about William Bentinck:
1. He took Coorg in 1834.
2. He took over the administration of Mysore.
3. He established universities for the first time in India.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: Bentinck took Coorg in 1834 and took over Mysore’s administration. The first universities were established in 1857 during Canning’s tenure, not during Bentinck’s tenure.
accepted.tq: Reject the later institutional development inserted into a list of genuine Bentinck measures.

accepted.s: Which Governor-General is associated with both the end of the Afghan War and the annexation of Sindh?
accepted.x: Ellenborough ended the Afghan War and annexed Sindh in 1843.
accepted.tq: Link two contemporaneous measures to their common Governor-General.

accepted.s: The Anti-Slavery Act of 1843 was enacted during the tenure of:
accepted.x: The Anti-Slavery Act was enacted in 1843 during Lord Ellenborough’s tenure.
accepted.tq: Use the year as an anchor to distinguish adjacent Governor-Generalships.

accepted.s: Which one of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
accepted.x: The Treaty of Lahore of 1846 was concluded during Hardinge I’s tenure. Auckland started famine relief, Hardinge I was associated with the Anti-Human-Sacrifice Act and Dalhousie with the Widow Remarriage Act.
accepted.tq: Identify the swapped Governor-General in a group of closely dated administrative measures.

accepted.s: Which of the following was NOT associated with Lord Dalhousie?
accepted.x: The Permanent Settlement was introduced by Cornwallis in 1793. Dalhousie was associated with the Doctrine of Lapse, the Caste Disabilities Removal Act and railway, post and telegraph development.
accepted.tq: Locate the historical outlier among measures of a single Governor-General.

accepted.s: Which one of the following is the correct chronological order of the Governor-Generals?
o: Warren Hastings, Cornwallis, Wellesley, Minto I
Cornwallis, Warren Hastings, Wellesley, Minto I
Warren Hastings, Wellesley, Cornwallis, Minto I
Minto I, Wellesley, Cornwallis, Warren Hastings
accepted.x: Warren Hastings served first, followed by Cornwallis, Wellesley and Minto I.
accepted.tq: Use the first and last positions to eliminate reversed and partially swapped sequences.

accepted.s: Who among the following served as Governor-General immediately after Sir John Shore?
accepted.x: Sir John Shore served from 1793 to 1798, and Wellesley succeeded him in 1798.
accepted.tq: Test succession through the boundary years of adjoining tenures.

accepted.s:
Arrange the following Governor-Generals in chronological order:
A. Sir George Barlow
B. Minto I
C. Cornwallis, second term
D. Wellesley
accepted.x: Wellesley served before Cornwallis’s second term; Cornwallis’s second term was followed by Sir George Barlow and then Minto I.
accepted.tq: Fix Wellesley as the earliest and Minto I as the latest, then arrange the middle pair.

accepted.s: Which Governor-General died at Ghazipur during his second term in office?
accepted.x: Cornwallis returned for a second term in 1805 and died at Ghazipur during that term.
accepted.tq: Use the exceptional second tenure to distinguish Cornwallis from the regular succession.

accepted.s: Which one of the following is the correct tenure of Marquess Hastings as Governor-General?
accepted.x: Marquess Hastings served as Governor-General from 1813 to 1823. The other periods correspond to Sir George Barlow, Minto I and Amherst respectively.
accepted.tq: Match the exact tenure with nearby consecutive administrations.

accepted.s: Which of the following statements is correct regarding William Bentinck’s tenure?
o: He served from 1823 to 1828 and was followed by Amherst.
He served from 1835 to 1836 and was followed by Auckland.
He served as Governor-General from 1828 to 1835 and became Governor-General of India from 1833.
He served as Governor-General only from 1833 to 1835.
accepted.x: Bentinck served from 1828 to 1835; after the Charter Act of 1833, he held the title Governor-General of India from 1833 onward.
accepted.tq: Separate the full tenure from the shorter period after the title changed.

accepted.s: The Vellore Mutiny of 1806 occurred during the tenure of:
accepted.x: The Vellore Mutiny occurred in 1806 during the tenure of Sir George Barlow.
accepted.tq: Use the event year to identify the Governor-General in office.

accepted.s: The Code of Gentoo Laws was compiled during the tenure of:
accepted.x: The Code of Gentoo Laws was prepared in 1776 during Warren Hastings’s tenure.
accepted.tq: Match the distinctive legal compilation with the correct early Governor-General.

accepted.s: The Ring Fence policy of Warren Hastings was intended primarily to:
o: Introduce direct British rule in Punjab
Create Awadh as a buffer state
accepted.x: The Ring Fence policy treated Awadh as a buffer state to protect British territories from external threats.
accepted.tq: Infer the purpose of a policy from its strategic description rather than its name alone.

accepted.s: Thuggee suppression with the assistance of Sleeman is associated with:
accepted.x: The suppression of Thuggee, with Sleeman’s assistance, took place during William Bentinck’s tenure.
accepted.tq: Apply the official–associate pairing without confusing it with military campaigns of later Governors-General.

accepted.s: The Public Works Department was established during the tenure of:
accepted.x: The Public Works Department was established during Lord Dalhousie’s tenure.
accepted.tq: Match the department with the Governor-General known for infrastructure expansion.

accepted.s: The liberation of the press in British India is associated with:
accepted.x: Sir Charles Metcalfe is associated with the liberation of the press during his brief tenure in 1835–36.
accepted.tq: Distinguish a press reform from the Charter Act and other administrative measures of nearby periods.

accepted.s: The Charter Act of 1813 was passed during the tenure of:
accepted.x: The Charter Act of 1813 was passed at the transition between Minto I and Marquess Hastings, whose tenure began in 1813.
accepted.tq: Handle an event falling at the boundary between two consecutive tenures.

accepted.s: The Treaty of Bassein of 1802 was concluded during the tenure of:
accepted.x: The Treaty of Bassein was concluded in 1802 during Lord Wellesley’s tenure, in the context of the Second Anglo-Maratha War.
accepted.tq: Match the treaty year with the Governor-General serving at that time.
accepted.sec: Governor-General - wars and treaties during tenure

accepted.s: The Anglo-Nepal War of 1814–1816 and the Treaty of Sugauli were associated with:
accepted.x: The Anglo-Nepal War took place during the tenure of Marquess Hastings, and the Treaty of Sugauli was concluded in 1816.
accepted.tq: Use the war period and treaty year together to identify the correct tenure.
accepted.sec: Governor-General - wars and treaties during tenure

accepted.s: The Treaty of Yandabo, which ended the First Anglo-Burmese War, was concluded during the tenure of:
accepted.x: The First Anglo-Burmese War occurred from 1824 to 1826 during Amherst’s tenure, and the Treaty of Yandabo transferred Assam, Manipur, Arakan and Tenasserim to the British sphere.
accepted.tq: Match the treaty with the war and the Governor-General in office.
accepted.sec: Governor-General - wars and treaties during tenure

accepted.s: Which one of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
accepted.x: The Second Anglo-Burmese War was fought during Dalhousie’s tenure. Auckland was associated with the First Anglo-Afghan War, Ellenborough with the war with Gwalior and Dalhousie with the Second Anglo-Sikh War.
accepted.tq: Find the campaign assigned to the wrong Governor-General among otherwise correct pairings.
accepted.sec: Governor-General - wars and treaties during tenure

accepted.s: The First Anglo-Sikh War and the Treaty of Lahore of 1846 occurred during the tenure of:
accepted.x: The First Anglo-Sikh War and the Treaty of Lahore occurred during Lord Hardinge I’s tenure.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the first Anglo-Sikh conflict from the later conflict under Dalhousie.
accepted.sec: Governor-General - wars and treaties during tenure

accepted.s: The office of Governor-General of Bengal was created by the:
accepted.x: The Regulating Act of 1773 created the office of Governor-General of Bengal, with Warren Hastings as its first holder.
accepted.tq: Match the constitutional title with the Act that created it.
accepted.sec: FIRST - Governor, Governor-General, Acts that changed the title

accepted.s: Which Act changed the title to Governor-General of India?
accepted.x: The Charter Act of 1833 changed the title to Governor-General of India, and William Bentinck was the first holder of that title.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the Act changing the territorial scope of the title from the later Act creating the Viceroyship.
accepted.sec: FIRST - Governor, Governor-General, Acts that changed the title

accepted.s: The title ‘Viceroy and Governor-General’ was created by the:
accepted.x: The Government of India Act of 1858 created the title Viceroy and Governor-General. Lord Canning was its first holder.
accepted.tq: Match the constitutional title with the statutory change that followed the transfer of power.
accepted.sec: FIRST - Governor, Governor-General, Acts that changed the title

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements:
1. Robert Clive was the first Governor of Bengal.
2. Warren Hastings was the first Governor-General of Bengal.
3. Lord Canning was the first Viceroy and Governor-General.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: Robert Clive was the first Governor of Bengal, Warren Hastings the first Governor-General of Bengal and Lord Canning the first Viceroy and Governor-General.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the first holders of three successive constitutional titles.
accepted.sec: FIRST - Governor, Governor-General, Acts that changed the title

accepted.s: William Bentinck was the:
o: First Governor-General of Bengal and first Viceroy
First Governor-General of India and last Governor-General of Bengal
First Governor of Bengal and first Governor-General of Bengal
First Viceroy and Governor-General and last Governor-General of India
accepted.x: William Bentinck was the first Governor-General of India and also the last Governor-General of Bengal after the title changed in 1833.
accepted.tq: Use the changeover between titles to identify the person occupying both transitional positions.
accepted.sec: FIRST - Governor, Governor-General, Acts that changed the title
